name: Multi-Armed Bandits
learningObjectives: Understand the multi-armed bandit problem and its applications
Learn the exploration-exploitation tradeoff in a simplified setting
Compare epsilon-greedy, UCB, and Thompson Sampling strategies
Understand regret as a performance metric for bandit algorithms
Recognize when to use bandit algorithms vs full reinforcement learning
Visualize cumulative rewards and regret over time

controls.label: Strategy
controls.tooltip: Choose the bandit algorithm strategy to use

controls.label: Number of Arms
controls.tooltip: Number of slot machines (arms) to choose from

controls.label: Number of Trials
controls.tooltip: Number of times to pull an arm (more trials = better learning)

controls.label: Epsilon (ε)
controls.tooltip: Exploration rate for epsilon-greedy strategy. Higher values explore more.

controls.label: Exploration Parameter (c)
controls.tooltip: Controls exploration in UCB. Higher values encourage more exploration.

visualizations.title: Cumulative Regret
visualizations.description: Total regret (difference from optimal) accumulated over time

visualizations.title: Arm Pull Distribution
visualizations.description: Number of times each arm was pulled

visualizations.title: True vs Estimated Rewards
visualizations.description: Comparison of true arm rewards and learned estimates

visualizations.title: Moving Average Reward
visualizations.description: Smoothed average reward over recent trials

metrics.name: Total Reward
metrics.description: Sum of all rewards received across all trials

metrics.name: Total Regret
metrics.description: Cumulative difference between optimal and actual rewards

metrics.name: Best Arm Found
metrics.description: The arm with highest estimated reward

metrics.name: Optimal Arm
metrics.description: The arm with highest true reward

metrics.name: Found Optimal
metrics.description: Whether the algorithm identified the best arm

metrics.name: Optimal Pull Rate
metrics.description: Percentage of trials that pulled the optimal arm
